# Voximov

> Voximov is a macOS app for recording, editing and mixing a voiceover on top of a video, with optional AI voiceover generated locally from a written script.

Video audio, the narrator's voice and music each sit on their own track, so they can be cut, moved and processed without touching the original files. The user records from the microphone at the playhead while the other tracks play, splits every track at the playhead on exact video frames, moves clips between tracks, and undoes any edit. Voice effects include high-pass, equalizer, compressor and expander presets, and loudness is normalized to -16 LUFS with a -1.5 dBTP true-peak ceiling by default. A mixer sets volume, pan, mute and solo per track. Export produces a WAV or MP3 of the mix or a single track, or an MP4 of the edited video with the full mix, encoded with the Mac's hardware H.264 encoder.

AI voiceover uses Kokoro, an open-source voice model that runs inside the app. The user drags a script clip across an audio track, types the line, and the speech is generated in place. There are 28 American and British English voices and a speed setting per track. Voximov reports words whose pronunciation it guessed, and accepts exact pronunciations written as phonemes, for example `[Voximov](/vˈɑksɪmɑv/)`. The voice model (about 100 MB) downloads once from Hugging Face; after that everything works offline. Nothing is uploaded and there is no account.

Voximov is for people who narrate their own videos: tutorials, game footage, product demos and course lessons. It works best for one narrator and a finished video, and it is not a full video editor. The interface is available in 13 languages. Voximov is in early access for Macs with Apple Silicon.
